To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression patterns of Fas ligands and transforming growth factor‐β in tumor cells and stromal cells are important for immune privilege during tumor progression.
FasL expression in tumor cells and TGF‐beta expression by tumor cells and stromal cells are involved in immune privilege in the tumor microen-vironment.
FasL and soluble FasL are associated with tumor progression and metastatic potential in various types of cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of FasL‐mediated tumor cell killing in tumor immunity, and the role of FASL and TGFβ in tumor progression.
the role of FasL‐mediated tumor‐induced apoptosis in the tumor micro‐environment.
the role of the Fas/FasL and the TGF‐β signaling pathways in tumor progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FasL and its receptor, Fas, are involved in the regulation of immune surveillance and that their expression is related to tumor progression and metastatic potential.
FasL and FasL‐mediated apoptosis are involved in tumor progression, and that FasL‐induced immunosuppression is a key factor for the development of cancer.
the FASL/Fas system is involved in tumor‐induced immune privilege, and the FasL/Fas ratio is a potential marker of the immune privilege of tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FasL is a potent tumor‐promoting molecule, and that TGF‐β is a key factor in the tumor‐promoting microenvironment.
the Fas‐FasL pathway is a key regulator of immune privilege and that FasL‐mediated immune suppression is involved in tumor progression and metastases.
the Fas/Fas ligand system is involved in immune privilege and tumor progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FasL and transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) are involved in the immune privilege of tumor progression and that the expression of Fas and FasL in cancer cells is regulated by the microenvironment.
the Fas ligand is a very powerful tool for studying the immune system.
FasL and its ligand, which are both expressed by tumor cells, play a role in the development and progression of cancer.
